submitter: silent_hero_logo_readers lane (the 267 round filed this bug; this is its fix)
rationale:
bugs_open/269, filed at this gate's own direction on 2026-08-12 (round ac23f2f7, bug_historian seat) and now fixed. The diagnosis bundle's 'Same-file signatures' section carries a heading that tells the verdict model these are handles it may put in next_scope. For a METHOD the handle it printed was the bare name, receiver discarded. That is ambiguous: analysis.spanOf matches a bare name against fi.Functions and takes the FIRST hit, so in a file where two types share a method name the bundle offered ONE handle for TWO different bodies. It does not error. It returns the wrong function's source, labelled as the right one, inside a section the verdict model treats as ground truth. That is worse IN KIND than the defect bugs_closed/261 fixed on the reader side: 261 failed loudly ('symbol not found', 301 times across 44 runs), this one succeeds with the wrong answer.

MEASURED 2026-08-13, control first because without it the measurement is unreadable. The query strips a '(Recv).' prefix to derive a bare name; if code_symbols did not store the parenthesised spelling the strip would be a no-op and every answer would still look like an answer. Of 1,175 kind='method' rows, 1,175 are stored parenthesised and 0 are not -- so the strip does real work and the spelling assumption holds exactly. The population where a bare handle can return the wrong body: 17 collision groups, 48 methods, 4.1% of all methods.
4.1% IS THE FLOOR OF THE HARM, NOT ITS RATE. In a group of n receivers a bare handle resolves to the first and is wrong for the other n-1. The worst groups here are SIX-way -- discovery_checks/check_integrity.go has six types sharing Name and six sharing Run -- so a bare handle there is wrong 5 times in 6. And pkg/diagnose/loop.go is itself in the list, (Outcome).String against (Tier).String: a diagnosis OF the diagnosis loop, which is what both 267 and 261 were, could have been handed the wrong String body with nothing in the bundle saying so. The interface-implementation shape that produces these groups (Name/Run across sibling check types, Error/Unwrap across error types) is exactly what a diagnosis reaches for when following a dispatch path.
WHAT THE MEASUREMENT DOES NOT CLAIM: not that 48 wrong bodies were served. Only that 48 methods sit in the population where the defect can fire, plus the per-group odds. Incidence is unmeasured -- the sibling section's per-file cap means many were never listed at all -- and would need a scan of diagnosis_artifacts.body for bare-handle lines, which this fix does not need.

The fix is candidate 1 from the bug file, calling analysis.CanonicalSymbolName rather than re-inlining the grammar. That helper was extracted in 17734b699 during the 267 round at FOUR seats' request (reuse_agent, constitution, tooling_provenance, architecture), so this fix is a CALLER of it, not a fourth copy. That leaves code_symbols_actions.go:598 as the one remaining independent producer of the spelling, which is exactly architecture_review/RFC_027's open question -- this narrows it and does not answer it.

THE HALF MOST EASILY GOT WRONG, and it is not the rendering. De-duplication. Suppressing every method that shares a bare name is the conservative-looking choice and it HIDES a sibling the model has not seen, inverting the purpose of a section that exists to show what retrieval missed. A bare scope entry resolves the way spanOf does -- first match in fi.Functions order -- so exactly one of the colliding methods is genuinely in scope. The fix tracks that in the same order spanOf scans, making the de-duplication exact rather than cautious. Reviewer: this is the arm to check hardest; its mutation (suppress all same-named) leaves the other two tests green.

plan.summary: The diagnosis bundle's sibling-signature section printed bare method names into a list it invites the model to name in next_scope, so a bare handle in a collision file silently resolved to the WRONG function body. Render the canonical (*Recv).Name handle via the existing analysis.CanonicalSymbolName, de-duplicate on it as well, and keep the de-duplication EXACT by tracking spanOf's first-wins rule rather than suppressing every same-named method. Measured population: 17 collision groups, 48 of 1,175 methods, worst groups six-way.

edits.rationale: Three defects in one loop. (a) The rendered handle used fn.Name, so a method's handle named two bodies whenever a file had a name collision -- now analysis.CanonicalSymbolName(fn), the helper this gate had extracted a day earlier, so there is no new copy of the grammar. (b) De-duplication keyed only on fn.Name, so a method in scope under its CANONICAL handle -- the common case, since scopeFromCodeResults concatenates the code_symbols spelling straight into scope -- was not suppressed and was listed as a sibling of itself. (c) The exactness half: a BARE scope entry resolves to the FIRST match in fi.Functions order, so only that one is in scope. Suppressing all same-named methods would be conservative and would hide a sibling the model has not seen. bareClaimed tracks first-wins in the same order spanOf scans, so no second copy of that resolution rule is introduced either -- it observes the order rather than re-deciding it.

THE FIXTURE MUST CONTAIN A COLLISION OR THESE TESTS ASSERT NOTHING -- every spelling resolves when only one candidate exists, which is exactly why this defect survived 261's fix. So: two types with a Handle method, the collision asserted as a fixture precondition before anything else, and the source run through the REAL analyser over a temp checkout rather than hand-described (hand-counted spans are how a fixture ends up agreeing with itself and nothing else). The load-bearing assertion is not a string match: it RESOLVES both offered handles through ReadSymbolBody and requires DIFFERENT bodies, which is precisely what the bare spelling could never satisfy. Three tests, three mutations, each failing alone: reverting the rendered handle fails all three; disabling the canonical de-dup fails only the §2a test; suppressing every same-named method fails only the exactness test.

grounded_in: bugs_closed/261 §8 follow-up 1, the original record: 'siblingSignatures renders fn.Name bare (diagnose_assemble_bundle_action.go:695), so the same method appears under a DIFFERENT spelling from the one the index section shows. The model is shown two grammars for one symbol and told to pick. It also means the in-scope dedup (named[fn.Name]) does not suppress a method that IS in scope under its receiver-qualified name, so it can be listed as a sibling of itself.'
the pre-fix line: 'line := fmt.Sprintf("- `%s:%s` — `%s`\n", f.Path, fn.Name, fn.Signature)' — fn.Name, receiver discarded
the section heading that makes it a handle and not a label: '## Same-file signatures (siblings of the in-scope symbols — name these in next_scope to read their bodies)'

analysis.spanOf's first-wins rule, which is what makes a bare handle ambiguous rather than merely ugly: 'for _, fn := range fi.Functions { if fn.Name != wantName { continue } ... return fn.StartLine, fn.EndLine, true }' — first match wins, no ambiguity check

CONTROL for the measurement, run before it: SELECT count(*) AS methods_total, count(*) FILTER (WHERE symbol LIKE '(%).%') AS parenthesised, count(*) FILTER (WHERE symbol NOT LIKE '(%') AS unparenthesised FROM code_symbols WHERE kind='method'; -> 1175 | 1175 | 0. The bare-name strip therefore does real work; a no-op strip would have produced a plausible wrong answer.

THE MEASUREMENT: SELECT count(*) AS colliding_name_groups, sum(n) AS methods_affected FROM (SELECT count(*) AS n FROM code_symbols WHERE kind='method' GROUP BY repo, path, regexp_replace(symbol,'^\(.*\)\.','') HAVING count(*) > 1) x; -> 17 groups, 48 methods of 1,175 (4.1%)

the worst groups, and why 4.1% understates the harm: discovery_checks/check_integrity.go has 6 receivers sharing 'Name' and 6 sharing 'Run'; check_news_feed.go 5 and 5; platform/errors/errors.go 2 sharing 'Error'; query_agent_definitions_actions.go 2 each sharing Next/Close/Err. In an n-way group a bare handle is wrong (n-1)/n of the time.

pkg/diagnose/loop.go is itself a collision file: (Outcome).String | (Tier).String. A diagnosis of the diagnosis loop — which bugs_open/267 and bugs_closed/261 both were — could be handed the wrong String body.

code_symbols schema read before the query rather than assumed (\d code_symbols): kind CHECK is ('func','method','struct','interface','alias','type','var','const'), so kind='method' is a valid filter; UNIQUE (repo, path, symbol), so one row per symbol per repo and no double-counting.
analysis.CanonicalSymbolName exists as of 17734b699, extracted during council round ac23f2f7 at four seats' request, so this fix is a caller and not a fourth inline copy of the spelling.
plan.risks: (1) THIS CHANGES BUNDLE TEXT for every bundle with a method sibling — a method that read 'path:Foo' now reads 'path:(*T).Foo'. That is the fix, not a side effect, and both spellings resolve through ReadSymbolBody (bugs_closed/261 taught splitReceiver to accept the bare form too), so no previously-working handle stops working. Reviewer: confirm you agree the churn is worth it for the 48-method population, given the failure it removes is a SILENT wrong body rather than an error. (2) The exactness arm is the one to check hardest. Suppressing every same-named method looks safer and would hide a sibling the model has not seen — the opposite of the section's purpose. Its mutation leaves the other two tests green, so only the dedicated test catches it. (3) bareClaimed relies on siblingSignatures iterating f.Functions in the SAME order spanOf scans fi.Functions. They are the same slice and both plain range loops, so this observes an order rather than re-deciding it — but if either ever sorts, the exactness arm silently mis-attributes which method is in scope. It would over-suppress one and list another, never produce a wrong body, so the failure mode is coverage not correctness. (4) Existing golden-literal tests (TestSiblingSignatures_ScopeEntryParsing) still pass unchanged: their fixtures carry no receivers, so plain functions render byte-identically. That is the negative control for over-reach. (5) NOT fixed: code_symbols_actions.go:598 remains an independent producer of the same spelling. Deliberate — live row-writing path, and RFC_027 is the open question about giving that grammar one owner. This fix narrows the RFC's scope from three producers to two.
